references.title: Ornela Radovicka, Antroposofia arbëreshe, rrëfime nga Caterina Bellusci, Dielli, 22 May 2024
references.scope: Primary first-person account of collecting Rina/Caterina Bellusci stories, songs and toponyms in local Frasnitë speech; repeated listening and Bellusci library recordings. No wholesale adoption of polemical or unsupported claims elsewhere in essay.

references.title: Comune di Civita: La lingua arbëreshe
references.scope: Municipal description of retained and innovative features, local varieties and contact with Italo-Romance; no frozen-language, population-total or universal-fluency claim.

references.title: Lukas D. Tsitsipis, A Linguistic Anthropology of Praxis and Language Shift, 1998
references.scope: Original linguistic anthropology, public abstract identifies Arvanitika as Albanian variety spoken in Greece. No access to full paywalled book claimed.

references.title: Stephanie Schwandner-Sievers, Albanians, Albanianism and the strategic subversion of stereotypes, 2008
references.scope: Original anthropology article, printed p. 56: Arnaut as Turkish ethnonym for Albanians; historical labels and representations.

references.title: Francesco Altimari, University of Calabria Albanological collections, 1979–2024
references.scope: Institutional archive account of 1979 Gangale donation, field recordings and subsequent cataloguing/transfer. This does not claim Rina’s particular performance is in that collection.

visuals.examples: Editorial prompts and concise researched terminology. No invented population, survival rate, language fluency or identity measurement.

meaningEvidence: Original creator caption identifies Rina Bellusci and emotional response to her Arbëresh song.
Complete original-audio ASR reviewed; spoken introduction 0–50.72 seconds names Civita/Frasnitë, Rina and Father Antonio Bellusci; remainder predominantly song.
Poster visually inspected and root source-video observations corroborate Rina singing seated indoors, holding Eduard’s hand while he wears a plis.
limitations: ASR is noisy, especially song. No lyrics or uncertain direct quotations are reproduced.
Song title, authorship, composition date and exact recording date are not independently established.
Caption hashtag Civita does not establish precise room/town of performance; article says Calabria and notes source introduction mentions both Civita and Frasnitë.
Radovicka’s first-person account supports Rina/Caterina identification and documented repertoire; no current age or universal community demographic is inferred.
Shared roots in creator commentary are personal affiliation, not a claim assigning present citizenship or national identity to all communities.
